verses.text: These are the proverbs of Solomon, David's son and Israel's king.
They're here to teach you wisdom and discipline and help you recognize words that carry real insight.
They'll train you to make wise moves and do what's right, just, and fair.
They give good sense to people who are easily led and give young people knowledge and judgment.
Even wise people can listen and learn more, and people with understanding can pick up solid advice.
They'll help you get the point of proverbs and stories and work out the sayings and riddles of wise people.
Knowledge starts with taking the LORD seriously and standing in awe of him. Fools look down on wisdom and discipline.
My son, listen when your father teaches you, and hold on to what your mother tells you.
Their teaching will look good on you, like a wreath on your head and a chain around your neck.
My son, if people doing wrong try to pull you in, don't go for it.
They might say, “Roll with us. Let's hide and wait to spill blood. Let's ambush somebody innocent for no reason.
Let's swallow them alive like the grave, whole like people dropping into the pit.
We'll grab all kinds of valuables and fill our houses with what we take.
Throw in with us. We'll all share the same pot.”
My son, don't go down that road with them. Keep your feet off their path.
They run straight toward evil and can't wait to spill blood.
You don't catch a bird by spreading the net where it can see you.
But these people are setting an ambush for their own blood. They're lying in wait for their own lives.
That's how it goes for anyone hungry for crooked gain. The stuff they grab ends up taking their lives.
Wisdom calls out in the street. She raises her voice in the public squares.
She calls above the noisy crowd and speaks up at the city gates.
“How long will you gullible people love being gullible? How long will mockers get a kick out of mocking, and fools hate knowing better?
Listen when I correct you and turn around. Look, I'll pour out my spirit on you and tell you what I have to say.
I called, and you refused to listen. I reached out my hand, and nobody paid attention.
You brushed off all my advice and wanted nothing to do with my correction.
So I'll laugh when disaster hits you. I'll mock when trouble catches up with you,
when it hits like a storm and disaster comes spinning in like a whirlwind, and you're gripped by distress and pain.
Then they'll call for me, but I won't answer. They'll look hard for me, but they won't find me.
They hated knowledge and chose to live without reverence for the LORD.
They wanted none of my advice and had nothing but contempt for my correction.
So they'll eat the fruit of the road they took and get their fill of their own schemes.
People who are easily led turn away, and it kills them. Fools get comfortable and careless, and it destroys them.
But whoever listens to me will live safely and rest easy, without being scared of harm.”
My son, take in what I tell you and keep my instructions close.
Tune your ears to wisdom and put your whole heart into understanding.
Call out for good judgment. Raise your voice and ask for understanding.
Look for it like you'd look for silver. Dig for it like buried treasure.
Then you'll understand what it means to stand in awe of the LORD, and you'll come to know God.
The LORD gives wisdom. Knowledge and understanding come straight from his mouth.
He saves up solid wisdom for people who live right. He's a shield for those who walk with integrity.
He guards the roads of justice and protects the path of his faithful people.
Then you'll understand what's right, what's just, what's fair, and how to recognize every good road.
Wisdom will settle in your heart, and knowing what's true will feel good deep down.
Good judgment will watch over you, and understanding will keep you safe.
They'll pull you away from evil roads and people who twist things with their words.
Those people leave the straight path to walk down dark roads.
They get excited about doing wrong and enjoy just how twisted evil can get.
Everything about their way of life is crooked. The paths they take are all over the place.
Wisdom will also save you from the foreign woman who tries to pull you in with smooth talk.
She's left the partner she had when she was young and forgotten the covenant she made before God.
Her house slopes down toward death. Her paths lead where the departed spirits are.
People who go to her don't make it back. They never reach the paths of life again.
So walk where good people walk and stick to the paths of those who do right.
People who live honestly will live in the land. People of integrity will get to stay.
But the wicked will be cut off from the land, and people who betray others will be ripped out by the roots.
My son, keep my teaching fresh in your mind. Hold on to my commands with your whole heart.
They'll add days and years to your life and bring you peace.
Keep kindness and truth close. Tie them around your neck like a necklace and carve them into your heart.
Then God and people will look on you with favor and see that you have good sense.
Trust the LORD with your whole heart. Don't prop yourself up on what you think you know.
Recognize him in everything you do, and he'll straighten out the road ahead of you.
Don't look at yourself and think you've got it all figured out. Stand in awe of the LORD, and walk away from evil.
That'll bring health to your body and nourish you right down to your bones.
Honor the LORD with what you own and give him the first share of everything you bring in.
Your barns will be packed, and your vats will spill over with fresh wine.
My son, take the LORD's discipline seriously. Don't get tired of him correcting you.
The LORD corrects the people he loves, like a father correcting a son who brings him joy.
Happy is the person who finds wisdom and gets hold of understanding.
What wisdom earns you beats silver. What she pays back is worth more than pure gold.
She's worth more than rubies. Nothing you could want comes close.
She holds a long life in her right hand and wealth and honor in her left.
Her ways are a joy to walk, and every road she takes leads in peace.
She's a tree of life to anyone who grabs hold of her. Everyone who holds on to her is happy.
The LORD laid the earth's foundations with wisdom and set the heavens in place with understanding.
By his knowledge the deep waters split open and the sky lets dew fall.
My son, keep your eyes on these things. Hang on to sound wisdom and good judgment.
They'll give you life deep down and grace like a necklace around your neck.
Then you can walk your road safely without tripping.
When you lie down, you won't be scared. You'll be able to lie down and sleep sweetly.
Don't be afraid when terror comes out of nowhere or when ruin hits the wicked.
The LORD will be the one you can count on. He'll keep your foot from getting caught.
When it's in your power to do something good for someone who is owed it, don't hold back.
Don't tell your neighbor, “Go away and come back. I'll give it to you tomorrow,” when you've got it right there.
Don't plot against your neighbor who lives beside you and trusts you.
Don't start a fight with someone for no reason when they haven't done you wrong.
Don't envy a violent person. Don't pick up any of their ways.
The LORD is disgusted by crooked people, but he shares his friendship with people who live honestly.
The LORD's curse rests on the home of the wicked, but he blesses the home of those who do right.
He mocks the mockers, but he gives grace to the humble.
The wise will inherit honor. Shame is what fools get lifted up to.
Sons, listen to what your dad is teaching you. Pay attention so you can get some understanding.
I'm giving you solid advice. Don't walk away from what I'm teaching you.
I was my father's son once, still small and my mother's only child in her eyes.
My dad taught me this: “Keep my words close to your heart. Follow my commands, and live.
Get wisdom. Get understanding. Don't forget what I tell you or wander away from it.
Don't leave wisdom behind, and she'll look after you. Love her, and she'll keep you safe.
Wisdom comes first, so go and get it. Even if it costs everything you've got, get understanding.
Value her, and she'll lift you up. Hold her close, and she'll bring you honor.
She'll set a wreath of grace on your head and hand you a beautiful crown.”
Listen, my son, and take my words in. You'll have many years to live.
I've shown you wisdom's way and led you along roads that run straight.
When you walk, nothing will hold your steps back. When you run, you won't trip.
Grab hold of instruction and don't let go. Keep it close. Your life depends on it.
Don't step onto the road the wicked take. Don't walk the way people who do evil walk.
Stay clear of it. Don't even go past it. Turn away and keep moving.
They can't sleep until they've done something wrong. They stay up until they've brought somebody down.
They eat wickedness like bread and drink violence like wine.
But the path of those who do right is like daybreak, getting brighter and brighter until it's full daylight.
The road of the wicked is pitch-dark. They have no idea what keeps tripping them up.
My son, pay attention to what I'm telling you. Lean in and listen.
Keep these words where you can see them, right in the middle of your heart.
They give life to whoever finds them and bring health to the whole body.
Be careful to guard your heart. That's where the springs of life flow from.
Cut out the twisted talk. Keep shady words far from your lips.
Look straight ahead. Keep your eyes on the road right in front of you.
Make the ground level where you step so every road you take is steady.
Don't veer right or left. Keep your feet away from evil.
My son, listen to the wisdom I'm giving you. Lean in to hear what I've learned.
That way you'll hold on to good judgment, and what you say will show that you know better.
The lips of a woman breaking her marriage vows drip with honey. Her words slide down smoother than oil.
But in the end she's bitter as wormwood and sharp as a blade that cuts both ways.
Her feet go down to death. Her steps head straight for the grave.
She doesn't give the road to life a thought. Her paths are crooked, and she doesn't even realize it.
So now, my sons, listen to me. Don't stray from what I've told you.
Take a route that stays far from her. Don't go anywhere near her front door.
Otherwise you'll hand your honor to other people and give your years to someone cruel.
Strangers will feast on your wealth, and all your hard work will make somebody else's household rich.
At the end you'll groan as your flesh wastes away and your body gives out.
You'll say, “I hated being taught. Deep down I couldn't stand having anybody correct me.
I didn't listen to my teachers. I wouldn't even hear out the people who tried to teach me.
Here I am at the edge of total ruin, right in front of everybody.”
Drink from your own cistern. Enjoy the fresh water flowing from your own well.
Should your springs spill out into the streets and your streams run through the public squares?
Keep that water for yourself. Don't share it with strangers.
May your spring be blessed, and take joy in the wife you married when you were young.
She's a loving doe, a graceful deer. Let her breasts satisfy you always, and let her love always sweep you away.
My son, why let another man's wife sweep you away? Why hold another woman close?
Everything people do is right in front of the LORD. He watches every road they take.
The wicked get caught in the evil they do. Their sin wraps around them like ropes and holds tight.
They'll die for lack of discipline. Their own foolishness will take them way off course.
My son, suppose you've put yourself up as security for your neighbor, or shaken hands on a promise to cover a stranger's debt.
Then your own words have caught you. That promise you made has you stuck.
Here's how to get free, my son. Your neighbor has you in his hands now, so go humble yourself and keep pleading with him.
Don't go to sleep. Don't even let your eyes close for a nap.
Get yourself free like a gazelle escaping a hunter, or a bird wriggling out of a trap.
Go watch an ant, you lazybones. Pay attention to how she lives and learn something. 🐜
She doesn't have a boss, a supervisor, or a ruler,
but she gets her food ready in summer and gathers what she'll eat at harvest.
How long are you going to lie there, lazybones? When are you getting out of bed?
“A little more sleep, a quick nap, just folding my hands and resting a bit.”
Then poverty will jump you like a robber, and need will come at you like somebody carrying a weapon.
A troublemaker who lives to do wrong goes around talking out of both sides of his mouth.
He winks, signals with his feet, and makes signs with his fingers.
His heart is twisted. He's always cooking up something evil and trying to get people fighting.
That's why disaster will hit him all at once. Just like that he'll break, and there'll be no putting him back together.
There are six things the LORD hates, seven that disgust him:
eyes that look down on people, a tongue that lies, hands that spill innocent blood,
a heart that cooks up wicked plans, feet that run straight into trouble,
a witness who lies about what happened, and somebody who gets brothers fighting.
My son, keep your father's command, and don't leave your mother's teaching behind.
Keep them tied close to your heart all the time. Wear them like a chain around your neck.
When you walk, they'll guide you. When you sleep, they'll watch over you. When you wake up, they'll have something to tell you.
The command is a lamp, and the teaching is a light. Correction that teaches you is the road to life.
It keeps you away from the woman who does wrong and the smooth talk of a wife who's straying.
Don't let desire for her beauty take over your heart, and don't let the way she looks at you reel you in.
A prostitute can leave you with nothing but a piece of bread. Another man's wife is hunting for your very life.
Can you scoop fire into your lap and keep your clothes from burning?
Can you walk across hot coals and come away without burning your feet?
That's how it goes when someone sleeps with his neighbor's wife. Whoever touches her will face punishment.
People don't look down on a thief for stealing food when he's hungry.
But if he gets caught, he has to pay back seven times what he took, even if it costs everything in his house.
A man who sleeps with another man's wife has no sense. He's destroying his own life.
He'll end up wounded and disgraced, and that shame won't wash off.
Jealousy makes her husband furious. When he comes for payback, he won't hold back.
He won't take any amount of money to let it go. You can pile on the gifts, and he still won't be satisfied.
My son, hold on to my words. Store my commands deep inside you.
Follow my commands and live! Protect what I teach you like you'd protect your own eyes.
Tie these words around your fingers. Carve them into your heart.
Tell wisdom, “You're my sister.” Treat understanding like family.
They'll keep you away from the woman who lures you in, the outsider with the smooth talk.
I was at my window, looking out through the lattice.
I saw some kids who didn't know better. One young guy in the group had no sense at all.
He walked down the street by her corner and took the road to her house.
The day was fading into evening, and the night closed in dark around him.
Then a woman came out to meet him, dressed like a prostitute and ready to play him.
She's loud and defiant. She can never stay home.
One minute she's in the street, the next she's in the square, lurking at every corner.
She grabbed him and kissed him, then looked him right in the face and said,
“I've got meat from my peace offerings. I kept my vows today.
That's why I came out to meet you. I've been looking everywhere for you, and here you are.
I've dressed my couch with woven covers, striped cloth made from Egyptian yarn.
I've scented my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
Come on, let's get our fill of love till morning. Let's lose ourselves in each other.
My husband's away from home. He's gone on a long trip.
He took a bag of money with him. He won't be back till the moon is full.”
She talked him right off course. She reeled him in with all that flattery.
He followed her on the spot, like an ox walking into the slaughterhouse, like a fool stepping into a noose,
till an arrow pierces his liver. He's like a bird rushing into a trap with no idea it's about to cost him his life.
So now, sons, listen to me. Pay attention to what I'm telling you.
Don't let your heart turn down her road. Don't wander onto her paths.
She's brought down a lot of people and left them wounded. The people she's killed could fill an army.
Her house is a road to the grave, heading down into the rooms of death.
Can't you hear Wisdom calling? Understanding is raising her voice!
She stands up high beside the road, right where the paths cross.
Next to the gates, at the doors where people enter the city, she calls out,
“Hey, people, I'm calling you! I want every human being to hear me.
If you're easily led, learn some good judgment! If you've been acting a fool, get some sense in your heart!
Listen up. I've got excellent things to say, and what comes out of my mouth is right.
I speak the truth. The thought of saying something wicked disgusts me.
Everything I say is fair and right. There's nothing twisted or shady in my words.
People with understanding can see that my words are clear. People who have found knowledge know my words are right.
Take my teaching over silver. Pick knowledge over the finest gold.
Wisdom beats rubies. Nothing you could want even comes close.
“I, Wisdom, live with good judgment. Go find knowledge and learn to think before you act.
To stand in awe of the LORD is to hate evil. I hate pride, arrogance, crooked talk, and the road that leads to evil.
I've got good advice and solid knowledge. Understanding and strength belong to me.
Through me kings reign and rulers make fair laws.
Through me rulers govern, along with nobles and everyone on earth who rules justly.
I love the people who love me. Anyone who seriously looks for me will find me.
I've got riches and honor, wealth that lasts, and prosperity.
What I grow is worth more than gold, even pure gold. My harvest is worth more than the finest silver.
I walk the road of doing right, right down the middle of the paths of justice,
so I can give wealth to the people who love me and fill up their treasuries.
“The LORD had me at the start of his work, before he did any of those things long ago.
I was set in place from eternity, right at the beginning, before the earth was even there.
I was born before the deep waters were there, before there were springs pouring out water.
Before the mountains got set in place, before the hills, I was born.
He hadn't made the earth or the fields yet, or even the first dust in the world.
When he set the heavens in place, I was right there. I saw him draw a circle across the face of the deep,
set the clouds up above and make the springs of the deep surge with strength.
I was there when he set a limit for the sea so its waters couldn't cross the line he gave them, and when he marked out the earth's foundations.
I was the craftworker right beside him. Day after day I was a delight, always celebrating in front of him,
celebrating in the whole world he made and taking joy in the people there.
“So now, my sons, hear me out. People who stick to my ways are blessed.
Listen when you're taught, and get wise. Don't push the lesson away.
Blessed is anyone who listens to me, who keeps watch at my gates day after day and waits by my doorway.
Whoever finds me finds life and receives favor from the LORD.
Whoever sins against me hurts their own soul. Everyone who hates me is in love with death.”
Wisdom built herself a house and carved out seven pillars for it.
She got the meat ready, mixed her wine, and set the table.
She sent out her young servants, and from the highest spots in town she calls,
“If you don't know any better, come on in!” To anyone short on sense, she says,
“Come get some of my bread! Drink the wine I mixed!
Leave those naive ways behind and live. Walk the road where you'll learn to understand.”
Correct a mocker, and you'll get insulted. Call out a wicked person, and you'll get abuse.
Don't correct somebody who just wants to mock you. They'll hate you for it. Correct a wise person, and they'll love you for it.
Give wise people a lesson and they'll get wiser. Teach people who do right and they'll learn even more.
Wisdom starts with standing in awe of the LORD. Knowing the Holy One is what it means to understand.
With me, you'll get more days and add years to your life.
If you're wise, you're the one who benefits. If you mock, you're the one who'll carry the cost.
Folly is loud and out of control. She doesn't know a thing.
She sits in her doorway on a seat high up in the city.
She calls to people passing by who are just going straight down their own roads.
“If you don't know any better, come on in!” To anyone short on sense, she says,
“Stolen water tastes sweet. Food you eat on the sly hits different.”
What they don't realize is that the dead are in there. Her guests are already deep in the grave.
These are Solomon's proverbs. A wise son makes his dad glad, but a foolish son breaks his mom's heart.
Riches you got by doing wrong do you no good, but doing what's right saves you from death.
The LORD won't let people who do right go hungry, but he pushes away what the wicked crave.
Work with lazy hands and you'll end up poor. Diligent hands bring in wealth.
A wise son brings in the crop in summer. A son who sleeps through harvest brings shame.
Blessings rest on the heads of people who do right, but violence covers the mouths of the wicked.
People remember those who did right with a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot.
Wise hearts take instruction. A fool who can't stop talking is headed for a fall.
Walk with integrity and you can walk secure. Take a crooked route and you'll get found out.
A sneaky wink can cause real hurt, and a fool who can't stop talking is headed for a fall.
What good people say is like a spring that gives life, but violence covers the mouths of the wicked.
Hatred gets fights going, but love covers every wrong.
Listen to somebody with good judgment and you'll hear wisdom. There's a rod for the back of somebody with no sense.
Wise people store up what they learn. A fool's mouth is always one step from disaster.
A rich person's money is like a fortified city. For poor people, poverty itself can bring them down.
The work of people who do right leads to life. What the wicked earn leads to sin.
Take correction and you're on the road to life. Brush it off and you'll lead others off course.
Hide your hate and you end up lying through your teeth. Spread slander and you're being a fool.
Keep piling on words and you're bound to say something wrong. A wise person knows when to stop talking.
The words of people who do right are like the finest silver. What's in the hearts of the wicked is worth little.
The words of people who do right feed many, but fools die because they lack sense.
The LORD's blessing is what makes people rich, and he doesn't pile trouble on top of it.
Doing wrong is fun to a fool. Wisdom is what makes a person with understanding happy.
What wicked people dread will catch up with them. What people who do right long for will be given to them.
When the whirlwind has blown through, the wicked are gone. People who do right stand firm forever.
Sending a lazy person on an errand is like getting vinegar on your teeth or smoke in your eyes.
Standing in awe of the LORD adds days to your life, but the wicked will have their years cut short.
The future brings joy for people who do right. The hopes of the wicked will come to nothing.
The LORD's way is a fortress to people who live honestly, but it brings ruin to people who do wrong.
People who do right will never be uprooted, but the wicked won't get to live in the land.
Wisdom comes from the mouths of people who do right. A tongue that twists things will be cut off.
People who do right know what words fit the moment. The wicked keep talking crooked.
The LORD can't stand rigged scales. Honest weights make him glad.
Pride shows up first, then shame follows. Wisdom comes with humility.
Honest people have their integrity to guide them. People who betray others get wrecked by their own crooked ways.
Money won't help when the day of wrath comes, but doing what's right saves from death.
A person who lives right has a straight road ahead. The wicked trip over their own wickedness.
Doing right gets honest people out of danger. Those who betray others get caught by their own evil cravings.
When wicked people die, their hopes die with them. Everything they expected from their power comes to nothing.
A person who does right gets pulled out of trouble, and a wicked person ends up in their place.
A godless person can wreck a neighbor with a few words, but people who do right get out of danger through knowledge.
The whole city celebrates when things go well for people who do right. When the wicked perish, people cheer.
A city rises when honest people bless it. What the wicked say can tear it down.
Looking down on your neighbor shows a lack of wisdom. A person with understanding knows when to keep quiet.
A gossip will spill what you told them in confidence. Someone you can trust knows how to keep a secret.
Without wise direction, a nation falls. With plenty of advisers, it can win.
Cover a stranger's debt and you'll pay for it. Refuse to put yourself up as security and you'll be safe.
A gracious woman earns honor. Violent men grab riches.
Being merciful does your own soul good. Being cruel brings trouble on your own body.
Wicked people earn a paycheck that won't hold up. Sow what's right and you'll reap a reward you can count on.
People who genuinely do right find life. People who chase evil find death.
The LORD can't stand a twisted heart. He takes joy in people whose lives are above blame.
Count on it, people who do evil will face punishment. The children of those who do right will be rescued.
A beautiful woman with no judgment is like a gold ring stuck in a pig's snout.
People who do right want what's good. What waits for the wicked is wrath.
Some people give freely and end up with even more. Others hold back more than they should and end up poor.
Generous people will thrive. When you give others water, you'll get water too.
People curse the one who keeps grain off the market, but they bless the one who sells it.
If you work hard to find what's good, you're looking for favor. If you go looking for evil, it'll find you.
Trust your money and you'll fall. People who do right will thrive like fresh green leaves.
Bring trouble on your own family and all you'll inherit is wind. A fool will end up serving someone with a wise heart.
What grows from a good person's life is a tree of life. A wise person wins people over.
Look, even people who do right get paid back here on earth. How much more will the wicked and sinful get what they've earned!
If you love being corrected, you love learning. Hating correction is just plain foolish.
A good person receives favor from the LORD. The LORD condemns people who cook up wicked plans.
Doing wrong will never give you solid footing. The roots of people who do right won't be shaken.
A wife with character is her husband's crown. A wife who brings disgrace is like rot deep in his bones.
People who do right think about what's fair. The advice of the wicked is loaded with lies.
Wicked people use words to set an ambush for blood. Honest people can talk their way out of danger.
The wicked get knocked down and vanish. The household of people who do right keeps standing.
People get credit for being wise. Someone whose thinking is twisted gets looked down on.
Better to be a nobody who can afford a servant than act important when you can't even afford bread.
People who do right care about their animals' lives. Even what the wicked call kindness turns out cruel.
Work your land and you'll have plenty of bread. Chase fantasies and you show you haven't got sense.
The wicked want the loot other evildoers have. People who do right have roots that thrive.
The wicked get trapped by the wrong things they say. People who do right make it out of trouble.
Good words bring good things back to you. What you do with your hands earns its own reward.
A fool looks at their own road and thinks it's right. A wise person hears people out.
A fool lets you know they're annoyed right away. Someone with good judgment lets an insult pass.
An honest person tells the truth on the stand. A false witness lies.
Some people speak without thinking and cut like a sword. Wise words help people heal.
Truthful words stand forever. A lie only lasts a moment.
People who plan evil carry deceit in their hearts. People who work for peace find joy.
Trouble won't overtake those who do right. The wicked will get their fill of evil.
The LORD can't stand lies. He takes delight in people who stay true to their word.
A sensible person doesn't broadcast everything they know. Fools can't help announcing how foolish they are.
People who work hard end up in charge. Laziness lands people in forced labor.
Anxiety weighs your heart down. A kind word can lift it.
Someone who does right is careful about who they befriend. The road the wicked take leads people off course.
A lazy person won't even cook what they caught. What diligent people have is precious.
There's life on the road of doing right. There's no death on that path.
A wise son listens when his dad teaches him. A mocker tunes out anyone who calls him out.
The good things a person says bring good things back to them. People who betray others are hungry for violence.
Watch what you say and you'll protect your life. Let every thought fly out of your mouth and you'll end up ruined.
Lazy people want plenty and get nothing. People who work hard get their fill.
People who do right hate lies. Wicked people bring shame and disgrace.
Doing what's right protects the road of a person with integrity. Wickedness knocks a sinner down.
Some people act loaded when they've got nothing. Others act broke when they're sitting on a fortune.
A rich person may have to buy their life back with their money. A poor person doesn't get those threats.
The light of people who do right burns bright, but the lamp of the wicked gets snuffed out.
Pride just starts arguments. You'll find wisdom with people willing to take advice.
Money gained by cheating dwindles away. Gather it through your own work and it grows.
When hope keeps getting put off, your heart gets sick. When what you've longed for finally comes, it's a tree of life.
Look down on instruction and you'll pay for it. Respect a command and you'll be rewarded.
A wise person's teaching is a spring of life that steers you away from death's traps.
Good sense earns favor. For people who break trust, the road is rough.
A sensible person learns what's going on before acting. A fool puts their foolishness on full display.
A wicked messenger gets into trouble. A messenger you can trust brings healing.
Turn down discipline and you'll end up poor and disgraced. Take correction seriously and you'll earn honor.
Finally getting what you've longed for feels sweet deep down. Fools can't stand the thought of giving up evil.
Spend time with wise people and you'll grow wise. Keep company with fools and you'll get hurt.
Trouble chases sinners down. People who do right are rewarded with good things.
A good person leaves something for their grandkids to inherit. A sinner's wealth gets stored up for people who do right.
The fields of poor people can grow plenty of food, but injustice sweeps it all away.
Whoever holds back the rod hates their son. Whoever loves him takes care to discipline him.
People who do right eat till they're satisfied. The wicked go away with empty stomachs.
A wise woman builds up her household. A foolish one tears hers down with her own hands.
People who live upright show reverence for the LORD. People who live crooked show contempt for him.
Foolish talk earns a rod across the back. Wise words can keep you safe.
Without oxen, the feeding trough stays clean. With the strength of an ox, you can bring in a big harvest.
An honest witness won't lie. A false witness pours out lies.

A whip for a horse, a bridle for a donkey, and a rod for a fool's back!
Don't answer a fool on their own foolish terms, or you'll end up just like them.
Answer a fool on their own foolish terms, or they'll walk away thinking they're wise.
Send a message with a fool and you might as well cut off your own feet and swallow trouble.
A proverb in a fool's mouth hangs useless like legs that can't carry their owner.
Giving a fool honor is like tying a stone into a sling.
A proverb in a fool's mouth is like a thorn bush in the hand of a drunk person.
Hire a fool or anyone who happens to walk past, and you're like an archer who wounds everybody.
A fool going back to the same foolishness is like a dog going back to its vomit.
See someone who thinks they've got all the wisdom? There's more hope for a fool than for them.
A lazy person says, “There's a lion in the road! A fierce lion is roaming the streets!”
A lazy person rolls around in bed like a door swinging on its hinges.
They put their hand in the dish and can't even be bothered to bring it back to their mouth.
A lazy person thinks they're wiser than seven people who actually know how to give a sensible answer.
Butt into a fight that isn't yours and you might as well grab a dog by the ears.
Picture someone out of control, shooting flaming torches and deadly arrows everywhere.
That's the person who tricks a neighbor, then says, “Come on, I was only joking!”
Run out of wood and the fire goes out. Take away the gossip and the fight dies down.
A person who loves to argue gets a fight going the way coal feeds hot embers and wood feeds a fire.
Whispered gossip tastes like little treats you swallow, and it drops deep inside you.
Passionate words from an evil heart are like silver waste smeared over a clay pot.
Someone who means harm hides behind their words while keeping evil tucked away in their heart.
When their talk sounds sweet, don't buy it. Their heart holds seven disgusting things.
They can hide their hatred behind lies for a while, but everyone at the gathering will see their wickedness exposed.
Dig a pit and you'll fall in yourself. Roll a stone and it'll come rolling back on you.
A lying tongue hates the people it hurts. A mouth that flatters people brings them to ruin.
Don't brag about tomorrow. You've got no idea what the day will bring.
Let someone else praise you. Let it come from a stranger's lips and leave your own mouth out of it.
A rock is heavy and a load of sand weighs you down. A fool who keeps provoking you weighs more than both.
Fury is cruel and anger can sweep you away. But who can stand up to jealousy?
Open correction is better than love somebody keeps hidden.
When a friend wounds you, they're being faithful to you. An enemy will smother you in kisses.
A person who's full turns their nose up at honeycomb. To somebody hungry, even bitter food tastes sweet.
A person who wanders away from home is like a bird that strays from her nest.
Perfume and incense cheer the heart. So does a friend's honest advice.
Don't drop your friend or your dad's friend. When disaster hits, don't head to your brother's house far away. A neighbor who's there beats a brother who's far off.
Be wise, my son, and make my heart glad. Then I'll have an answer for the person giving me grief.
Someone with good sense spots danger and takes cover. People who don't know better keep going and pay for it.
Take the coat of someone who puts themselves up as security for a stranger. Hold it when they do it for a woman who strays.
Shout a blessing at your neighbor first thing in the morning and they'll take it as a curse.
A wife who's always picking a fight is like a drip that won't quit on a rainy day.
Trying to hold her back is like trying to hold the wind or grab oil in your right hand.
Iron sharpens iron, and one friend sharpens another.
Take care of a fig tree and you'll get to eat its figs. Look after your master and you'll be honored.
Water shows you your face. Your heart shows who you are.
The grave and the place of destruction never get full. Your eyes never get enough either.
A refining pot tests silver, and a furnace tests gold. Praise is what puts a person to the test.
You could pound a fool in a mortar with a pestle right along with the grain, and you still wouldn't get the foolishness out.
Know what shape your flocks are in. Pay close attention to your herds.
Money doesn't last forever. Even a crown won't stay in the family through every generation.
The hay gets taken in, new grass grows, and the grass on the hills gets gathered.
Your lambs give you clothes, and your goats can pay for a field.
You'll have enough goats' milk to feed yourself and your family and keep your servant girls fed too.
The wicked run when nobody's even after them. People who do right stand bold as a lion. 🦁
When a country rebels, rulers come and go. A leader with understanding and knowledge can keep things steady.
A poor person who pushes other poor people around is like pounding rain that leaves no crops behind.
People who ditch the law cheer on the wicked. People who keep it stand up to them.
People who do evil don't get justice. People who seek the LORD understand it through and through.
Better to be poor and live with integrity than get rich while living crooked.
A son who keeps the law is wise. Hang around with people who live to stuff themselves and you'll shame your father.
Pile up wealth by charging outrageous interest and you're saving it for someone who cares about the poor.
Turn away when the law is read and even your prayers become disgusting.
Lead honest people down an evil road and you'll fall into your own trap. People who live above blame will inherit good things.
A rich person can think they're so smart. A poor person with understanding sees right through them.
When people who do right win, there's great glory. When the wicked rise, people go into hiding.
Cover up your sins and things won't go well. Own up to them and leave them behind and you'll find mercy.
Blessed is the person who always walks with reverent fear. Harden your heart and you'll fall into trouble.
A wicked ruler over helpless people is like a roaring lion or a bear charging straight at them.
A tyrant has no judgment. A ruler who hates crooked gains will live a long time.
Someone weighed down by the guilt of spilling blood will be on the run until death. Nobody will stand behind them.
Live above blame and you'll be kept safe. Take crooked roads and you'll go down without warning.
Work your land and you'll have food to spare. Chase fantasies and you'll get your fill of poverty.
A faithful person will be rich in blessings. Someone desperate to get rich will face punishment.
Playing favorites is wrong, but a person can still be tempted to do wrong for one piece of bread.
A stingy person races after riches without realizing poverty is waiting for them.
In the end, someone who calls a person out will find more favor than someone who flatters them.
Rob your father or mother and say, “I'm doing nothing wrong,” and you've teamed up with a destroyer.
Greed starts fights. Trust the LORD and you'll thrive.
Trusting your own judgment alone is foolish. Walk with wisdom and you'll be kept safe.
Give to people who are poor and you won't go without. Close your eyes to them and you'll get plenty of curses.
When the wicked rise, people go into hiding. When the wicked perish, people who do right thrive.
Keep getting corrected and digging in your heels, and you'll break without warning. There'll be no fixing it.
When people who do right thrive, everybody celebrates. When the wicked rule, everybody groans.
Love wisdom and you'll make your dad glad. Hang around with prostitutes and you'll blow through your money.
A king gives his country solid ground by judging fairly. Take bribes and you tear it down.
Flatter your neighbor and you're spreading a net right where they're about to step.
Evil people get caught in their own sin. People who do right can sing and celebrate.
People who do right care whether poor people get justice. The wicked can't be bothered to know about it.
Mockers get a whole city worked up. Wise people cool down the anger.
If a wise person takes a fool to court, the fool rages or laughs it off. There's no settling it in peace.
People out for blood hate somebody who lives with integrity. They go after the lives of honest people.
A fool lets all their anger out at once. A wise person keeps theirs under control.
If a ruler listens to lies, every official under them will be wicked.
The poor person and the one who oppresses them have this in common. The LORD gave both of them eyes that see.
A king who judges poor people fairly will have a throne that stands forever.
The rod and a correction can teach wisdom. Leave a child to do whatever they want and they'll shame their mother.
When the wicked multiply, so does sin. People who do right will see them fall.
Correct your son and he'll give you peace. He'll bring you joy deep down.
Without revelation people throw off every restraint. Blessed is whoever keeps the law.
Words alone won't correct a servant. They can understand what you say and still give you no response.
See somebody who talks before they think? There's more hope for a fool than for them.
Pamper a servant from the time they're young and they'll end up like a son.
An angry person gets fights going. A person ruled by fury piles up sin.
Pride will bring you low. A humble spirit will win you honor.
Team up with a thief and you're working against your own life. You're put under oath and still don't dare say what you know.
Fear of people will trap you. Put your trust in the LORD and you'll be kept safe.
Lots of people try to get on a ruler's good side. The justice you get comes from the LORD.
Dishonest people can't stand those who do right. Honest people can't stand the wicked.
These are the words of Agur, Jakeh's son. This is the revelation he spoke to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal.
“Honestly, I know less than anybody. I haven't even got an ordinary person's understanding.
I haven't learned wisdom, and I don't know the Holy One.

Who went up into heaven and came back down? Who caught the wind in their fists? Who wrapped the waters in their coat? Who set up every end of the earth? What's his name, and what's his son's name, if you know?
“Every word God speaks is flawless. He's a shield for anyone who runs to him for safety.
Don't tack anything on to his words. He'll correct you, and you'll be exposed as a liar.
“I'm asking you for two things. Please don't refuse me before I die.
Keep dishonesty and lies far away from me. Give me enough without making me poor or rich. Feed me what I need.
Otherwise I might get full, turn my back on you, and say, ‘Who's the LORD?’ Or I might get so poor I steal and drag my God's name through the dirt.
“Don't trash a servant to their master. The servant might curse you, and you'll be held guilty.
There's a generation that curses their dads and has no blessing for their moms.
There's a generation that looks at itself and sees nothing dirty, while their filth hasn't even been washed off.
There's a generation that looks down on everybody. Just look how high they lift their eyes!
There's a generation with teeth like swords and jaws like knives, eating the poor off the earth and wiping needy people out of society.
“The leech has two daughters, and all they say is, ‘Give! Give!’ There are three things that never get full, four that never say, ‘Enough!’
The grave, a womb that can't bear children, ground that never gets enough water, and a fire that never says, ‘Enough!’
“An eye that mocks its father and sneers at obeying its mother will be picked out by the ravens of the valley and eaten by young eagles.
“There are three things that amaze me, four I just can't figure out.
How an eagle moves through the air, how a snake moves across a rock, how a ship moves through the sea, and how a man makes his way with a young woman.
“Here's how a woman who breaks her marriage vows acts. She eats, wipes her mouth, and says, ‘I haven't done anything wrong.’
“Three things make the earth shake. Four are more than it can bear.
A servant who becomes king, a fool with a belly full of food,
a woman nobody loves who gets married, and a servant girl who inherits what was her mistress's.
“Four things on earth are tiny, but unbelievably wise.
Ants aren't strong, but they get their food together in summer.
Rock hyraxes are weak little creatures, but they make their homes in the rocks.
Locusts have no king, but they all move forward in ranks.
You can catch a lizard in your hands, yet there it is in kings' palaces.
“There are three things that stride with dignity, four that walk like they own the road.
The lion, strongest of the animals, turns away for nobody.
Then there's the greyhound, the male goat, and a king nobody dares rise up against.
“If you've acted foolishly by showing off, or you've been thinking up something evil, put your hand over your mouth.
Churn milk and you get butter. Twist a nose and you get blood. Keep pushing someone's anger and you'll get a fight.”
These are King Lemuel's words, the revelation his mother taught him.
“Oh, my son! The son I carried! The son I made vows for!
Don't spend your strength chasing women or live in ways that bring kings down.
Lemuel, wine isn't for kings. Rulers shouldn't be asking, ‘Where's the strong stuff?’
They might drink, forget the law, and twist the justice owed to someone who's suffering.
Give strong drink to the person who's about to die, and wine to those bitter with grief.
Let them drink and forget how poor they are, and stop remembering their misery.
Speak up for people who can't speak, and take up the case of everyone who's been left with nobody.
Open your mouth, judge fairly, and make sure poor and needy people get justice.”
Who can find a woman of real character? She's worth far more than rubies.
Her husband trusts her with his whole heart. He'll have everything he needs to prosper.
She does him good and never harm, all the days of her life.
She goes looking for wool and flax and gets right to work with her hands.
She's like a fleet of merchant ships, bringing food home from far away.
She gets up while it's still dark and gives her household food, with portions for her servant girls.
She checks out a field and buys it. With what her own hands earned, she plants a vineyard.
She gets herself ready for hard work and makes her arms strong.
She sees that what she sells turns a profit. Her lamp is still burning at night.
She reaches for the distaff and takes hold of the spindle.
She opens her arms to poor people and reaches out to anyone in need.
Snow doesn't scare her on account of her household. Everybody at home is dressed in scarlet.
She makes her own woven coverings. She wears fine linen and purple.
Her husband is respected at the city gates, where he sits with the elders of the land.
She makes linen clothes to sell and supplies the merchant with sashes.
She wears strength and dignity like clothes and laughs at the days ahead.
When she speaks, wisdom comes out. She teaches with kindness.
She keeps an eye on how things go at home and never sits around eating the bread of idleness.
Her children stand up and call her blessed. Her husband praises her too.
“Lots of women do noble things, but you've gone above them all.”
Charm can fool you, and beauty won't last. A woman who stands in awe of the LORD deserves praise.
Give her what her hands have earned! Let the work she's done speak her praise at the city gates!
